title: Natural comparison of right-pinched and arrow mapping spaces
statement:
Use quasicategories, internal functor simplicial sets and the right-pinched mapping space $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal D}(x,y)$ of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. For a quasicategory $\mathcal D$ and vertices $x,y$, define the arrow mapping space
$$U_{\mathcal D}(x,y)=\{x\}\times_{\mathcal D,\operatorname{ev}_0}\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,\mathcal D)\times_{\operatorname{ev}_1,\mathcal D}\{y\}.$$
Both $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal D}(x,y)$ and $U_{\mathcal D}(x,y)$ are Kan complexes. Precomposition in degree $n$ with the map $\Delta^n\times\Delta^1\to\Delta^{n+1}$ induced by $(a,0)\mapsto a$ and $(a,1)\mapsto n+1$ (interchanging the two product factors to use the internal-functor convention) defines the right-pinch inclusion
$$j_{\mathcal D,x,y}:\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal D}(x,y)\longrightarrow U_{\mathcal D}(x,y).$$
This is a homotopy equivalence, natural under every simplicial functor $\mathcal D\to\mathcal D'$ carrying $x,y$ to the specified endpoints.

source.place: Proposition 4.6.5.10, right-pinch assertion, with Construction 4.6.5.1 (01KX), Proposition 4.6.5.5 (01L0), and the pinch maps of Construction 4.6.5.7. Kerodon tag 01L5 (not the unrelated Stacks tag); read online, not archived under literature/.

proof.text: Define $S_y$ to have $n$-simplices $\sigma:\Delta^{n+1}\to\mathcal D$ with last vertex $y$, operators $\sigma\mapsto\sigma\alpha^+$ for $\alpha:[m]\to[n]$, where $\alpha^+$ agrees with $\alpha$ on $[m]$ and sends $m+1$ to $n+1$, and projection $p:S_y\to\mathcal D$ given by the entire initial face. Set $T_y=\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,\mathcal D)\times_{\operatorname{ev}_1,\mathcal D}\{y\}$ with source projection $q$. The degreewise fibers $p^{-1}(x)$ and $q^{-1}(x)$ are exactly $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal D}(x,y)$ and $U_{\mathcal D}(x,y)$: the first fiber makes the whole initial simplex constant at $x$, and the second fixes both endpoint simplices. This uses the explicit mapping-space and functor definitions of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], including all degeneracies.

source.place: Construction 4.6.5.1 and the degreewise definitions of the right slice and ordinary arrow fiber

proof.text: The projection $p$ is a right fibration. Indeed, for a right horn $\Lambda_i^m\hookrightarrow\Delta^m$, $m\geq1$ and $0<i\leq m$, a lifting square for $p$ gives maps on the faces of $\Delta^{m+1}$ as follows: the bottom simplex supplies the face opposite the last vertex; for each $j\neq i$ with $0\leq j\leq m$, the $j$th slice face supplies the face opposite $j$, and the last vertex is $y$. Their intersections agree by the lifting-square identities. These are precisely all faces except the $i$th, hence a map $\Lambda_i^{m+1}\to\mathcal D$. Since $0<i<m+1$, the quasicategory horn axiom of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] fills it. This gives the required slice lift. Also $S_y$ is a quasicategory: project any inner horn to $\mathcal D$, fill there, then use the just-proved right-fibration lifting property over that filler. This includes $m=1,i=1$, whose coned horn is the inner horn $\Lambda_1^2$.

source.place: Proposition 4.3.6.1, singleton right-slice case; explicit inner-horn argument

proof.text: Apply [lem-coef-infinity-arrow-target-right-fibration] to $\mathcal D$ and $T=y$. Its displayed arrow pullback is exactly $T_y$, and it says that its source projection $q$ is a right fibration. This verifies the same nonzero-index horn convention used in step 2. The total simplicial set $T_y$ is a quasicategory: for an inner horn in $T_y$, fill its image in $\mathcal D$ and lift that filler using $q$. Thus both vertical maps $p,q$ are right fibrations between quasicategories over the same quasicategory $\mathcal D$.

Use the unconditional Kan-fiber assertion of [lem-coef-infinity-right-fibration-fibers] on $p$ and $q$ at $x$. Its hypotheses were checked in steps 2 and 3; the identifications of step 1 show that these two Kan fibers are exactly the two mapping spaces in the statement. There is no requirement that a fiber contain a vertex.

source.place: Corollary 4.4.2.3, applied to the two right fibrations

proof.text: The slice comparison of [lem-coef-infinity-slice-arrow-equivalence] supplies an equivalence $\delta_y:S_y\to T_y$ over $\mathcal D$. In degree $n$ its formula is $\delta_y(\sigma)=\sigma\rho_n$, with $\rho_n(a,0)=a$ and $\rho_n(a,1)=n+1$; restriction to the initial layer gives $q\delta_y(\sigma)=\sigma|_{\Delta^n}=p(\sigma)$, so it induces a map of the strict fibers. On that fiber its formula is the specified $j_{\mathcal D,x,y}$, including the factor swap in the internal-functor convention. Apply the equivalence-on-fibers assertion of [lem-coef-infinity-right-fibration-fibers] to $h=\delta_y$, the identity base functor, and the right fibrations from steps 2 and 3. It proves that this actual map $j_{\mathcal D,x,y}$ is a homotopy equivalence of the Kan complexes in step 4.

source.place: Proposition 4.6.5.10, right-handed version of the displayed slice/arrow fiber argument

proof.text: For every monotone $\alpha:[m]\to[n]$, the maps used above satisfy $\rho_n(\alpha\times\mathrm{id})=\alpha^+\rho_m$: at $(a,0)$ both sides give $\alpha(a)$ and at $(a,1)$ both give $n+1$. Thus precomposition defines a simplicial map, with no choices of fillers involved. Moreover, $\rho_n$ has a section induced by the monotone map sending $a\leq n$ to $(a,0)$ and $n+1$ to $(n,1)$. Hence $\sigma\rho_n$ determines $\sigma$ in each degree, so $j$ is degreewise injective, as its name inclusion indicates. The sections need not be natural in $n$ for this injectivity argument. If $H:\mathcal D\to\mathcal D'$ carries $x,y$ to $x',y'$, then on every simplex $H(\sigma\rho_n)=(H\sigma)\rho_n$. Hence $U(H)\,j_{\mathcal D,x,y}=j_{\mathcal D',x',y'}\operatorname{Map}(H)$ strictly in every degree. The construction is therefore natural for all the simplicial functors in the statement; no natural choice of inverse homotopy equivalences is asserted or needed.

lean.statement: theorem right_pinch_comparison : ∃ j : ∀ (D : SSet.{u}) [Quasicategory D] (x y : D _⦋0⦌), mappingSpace D x y ⟶ arrowMappingSpace D x y, ∀ (D : SSet.{u}) [Quasicategory D] (x y : D _⦋0⦌), (∀ (n : SimplexCategoryᵒᵖ) (s : (mappingSpace D x y).obj n), MonoidalClosed.uncurry (SSet.yonedaEquiv.symm ((j D x y ≫ arrowMappingSpaceInclusion D x y).app n s)) = rightPinchPrism n.unop.len ≫ SSet.yonedaEquiv.symm s.1) ∧ KanComplex (mappingSpace D x y) ∧ KanComplex (arrowMappingSpace D x y) ∧ (∃ r : arrowMappingSpace D x y ⟶ mappingSpace D x y, Nonempty (SSet.Homotopy (j D x y ≫ r) (𝟙 _)) ∧ Nonempty (SSet.Homotopy (r ≫ j D x y) (𝟙 _))) ∧ (∀ (E : SSet.{u}) [Quasicategory E] (f : D ⟶ E), j D x y ≫ arrowMappingSpaceInclusion D x y ≫ (ihom Δ[1]).map f = mappingSpaceMap f x y ≫ j E (f.app _ x) (f.app _ y) ≫ arrowMappingSpaceInclusion E (f.app _ x) (f.app _ y))
lean.note: The existential supplies a family of canonical inclusions, uniquely specified in every degree by the displayed prism formula after the monomorphic arrow-space inclusion. It has no arbitrary comparison-map hypothesis. The conclusion gives actual inverse maps and simplicial homotopies, not merely weak homotopy equivalence. Helpers belong to this node; the sole postponed theorem is this node itself.
